skript.thema: Gemini: Gemini Tips Most Users Miss

teile.name: Local edits
teile.text: Want to fix just one detail in a photo? Gemini supports local edits: specific changes to parts of an image.
teile.szene: Black-haired man in black leather jacket and glowing cyan glasses, painted open-world-game poster style, studies a framed photo at a city rooftop studio, one hand hovering over a single detail, medium shot, warm dusk light.

teile.name: Upload and edit
teile.text: Open an image Gemini generated, or upload your own photo. Then type the change you want in the text box.
teile.szene: Painted open-world-game style, cyan-glasses presenter in leather jacket sits at a street-side workbench, typing thoughtfully on a laptop while holding one printed snapshot, close medium shot, neon evening light, no readable text.

teile.name: Redo with Pro
teile.text: Need text or an infographic? Paid subscribers can click Redo with Pro. Google says Pro adds detail, especially for text.
teile.szene: Painted urban game-poster scene: the cyan-glasses presenter leans toward a large poster being unrolled by a worker in a graffiti-lined workshop, intrigued expression, wide shot, golden light.

teile.name: Daily quota limit
teile.text: So what's the catch? If you reach your daily Nano Banana 2 image quota, you can't redo images with Pro.
teile.szene: Painted open-world-game style, cyan-glasses presenter in leather jacket stops mid-step at a closed metal shutter on a night street, frowning, hand raised, medium shot, cool blue streetlight.

teile.name: Download size
teile.text: Downloads vary too. Google lists 2K resolution with a Google AI plan, or 1K without one. Plan matters here.
teile.szene: Painted game-poster style, cyan-glasses presenter holds a large blank print up to the light, comparing its crispness, in a tidy loft studio, medium close shot, soft window light.

teile.name: One specific edit
teile.text: So that one detail? Upload the photo, describe only that change, then review the result before you download it.
teile.szene: Painted open-world-game style, cyan-glasses presenter in leather jacket points to one small spot on a printed photo at a cafe table, then smiles, over-the-shoulder medium shot, warm morning light.

teile.name: Call to action
teile.text: Be sure to like, share and save this video.
teile.szene: Painted open-world-game poster style, cyan-glasses presenter in black leather jacket smiles with a thumbs-up on a city rooftop at sunset, medium shot, calm sky above and open space below.

A zoom, crop, subtitle change or decorative background does not count as a new motif. Never fill missing images with candles, unrelated stock or background-only frames.
Show the main image prominently; avoid tiny repeated photos in a mostly empty vertical frame. Preserve genuine evidence and important image details.
For AI Tools Explained identify the exact tool briefly, then show genuine interface views and different source-supported examples. Never present stock or an illustration as a real tool result.
Use original urban painted open-world-game poster styling for fictional scenes and presenters; no copied game characters. Match narrated action and era.

Clear speech and readable captions alone do not make a professional video. Inspect useful motif changes and narration-image alignment over the entire video. Missing main imagery is a substantial defect.

Explain the human task, the source-supported action and a concrete limit. A generic trending-tools question failed story review twice; prefer a specific visual workflow.

hooklabor.alt: Want to fix just one detail in a photo?
kandidaten: One photo, one tiny flaw, and you don't have to start over.
Most people regenerate the whole image when only one detail is wrong.
Gemini can change one part of your photo and leave the rest alone.
Why redo an entire image to fix one small thing?
She uploaded her photo and changed just one detail, nothing else.
hooklabor.begruendung: Candidate 2 directly addresses a common pain point that the rest of the script immediately solves by introducing Gemini's local editing feature, unlike purely clickbaity or overly vague alternatives.

Generate & edit images with Gemini Apps - Computer - Gemini Apps Help Skip to main content
Generate & edit images with Gemini Apps
You can create captivating images in seconds with Nano Banana 2. From work, play, or anything in between, Gemini Apps can help you generate and refine images to help bring your imagination to life. For paid subscribers, Nano Banana Pro is also available to regenerate images.
Important: When you generate images with Gemini Apps, remember that you agreed to Google's Terms of Service , including the Prohibited Use Policy . Be sure not to violate others' copyright or privacy rights. Use your discretion before you rely on, publish, or use content that Gemini Apps generate. Users with a work or school account may be subject to different terms depending on the license type. Learn more about how to use Gemini Apps with your work or school Google Account .
This feature’s availability in any specific Gemini app is also limited to the supported languages and countries of that app.
To use this feature, you must be signed in to Gemini Apps. Learn how to sign in to Gemini Apps .
To meet the age requirements to use this feature with a personal account.
To generate and edit images, you must be 18 or over
To generate images, you must be 13 (or the applicable age in your country ) or over.
If you are signed in to a school account, you may be subject to different access restrictions.
Key features of Nano Banana 2
Improved world knowledge: create diagrams and infographics with more accurate info.
Character consistency: Maintain the look of a person or character across various generated images, including the ability to combine multiple images to blend scenes or ideas.
Local edits: Making quick and specific changes to parts of an image.
Better text rendering: Add text to images with more accurate spelling, for all supported languages.
Enhanced instruction following: The model can follow more complex requests, to capture details.
High output quality:  Preview images at high resolution. Download images at at 2K resolution with a Google AI plan or at 1K without an AI plan.
Nano Banana 2 is ideal to create personalized images such as when you want to view yourself with different hairstyles, picture yourself in different scenes or create memes.
If you’re in the US and meet other requirements, Nano Banana 2 can also use Personal Intelligence to create and edit images tailored entirely to you. Learn how Gemini personalizes images with Personal Intelligence .
To use a different Nano Banana model, switch your Gemini model before you create your image request.   Learn how to switch models .
Nano Banana offers different models designed for various needs.
Nano Banana 2 Lite: This option is used when the Gemini model is set to Flash-Lite. It  is optimized for speed. It is ideal for quick images and basic ideas. It isn’t designed for multiple image references or for multiple edits.
Nano Banana 2: This option is selected when you make an image request with the Gemini model set to Flash or Pro. It  balances speed with higher image quality, more world knowledge, and reliable text rendering. It can accept multiple reference images.
Nano Banana Pro: Available with a Google AI Plan, this option is available when you have the Gemini model set to Pro and want  to redo an image when additional detail is needed. It has the highest level of world knowledge, advanced text and language capabilities, higher consistency, and more precise creative control.
On your computer, go to gemini.google.com .
On the top left, click Open Sidebar   Images .
Choose a template or enter your prompt to generate an image with Nano Banana 2. Check tips for image generation prompts .
Generate an image of a futuristic car driving through an old mountain road surrounded by nature
Create an image of a dog riding a surfboard
Create an image of a jungle with a river in a splashy watercolor style
Create and use an avatar with Nano Banana
You can record your face and voice to create your avatar to use when you create images with Nano Banana.
Your avatar lets you create custom images or yourself without the need to upload a photo each time.
Learn how to create and use an avatar in Gemini Apps .
Edit images with Nano Banana 2
Important: Editing images isn't available to users under 18.
With Nano Banana 2, there are a few ways that you can edit images. For example, you can:
Edit an image that you generated in Gemini Apps.
Upload an image and ask Gemini to make edits.
Upload multiple images and ask Gemini to create a new image based on your uploaded images.
Find examples of how you can edit images .
On the top left, click Open Sidebar   Library  .
Find the image you want to edit and click it.
Tip: You can also upload an image from your device that you want to edit. Learn how to upload files in Gemini Apps .
In the text box at the bottom, enter your prompt.
Tip: You can upload an image to edit or ask Gemini to edit a generated image.
Redo an image with Nano Banana Pro
Paid subscribers can use Nano Banana Pro to regenerate an image. Nano Banana Pro can provide additional detail, especially for images that use text rendering or for infographics. To use Nano Banana Pro:
Create an image with Nano Banana 2 or Nano Banana 2 Lite.
At the bottom right, click More      Redo with Pro .
Important:  If you reach your daily quota of Nano Banana 2 images, you can’t redo any additional images with Nano Banana Pro.
Connect Google Photos to edit & transform photos
Important: This feature is only available to users 18 and over in the US. You must be signed in to your personal Google Account to use it. The Google Photos connected app currently isn’t available in some US regions.
To use Nano Banana to edit and transform your photos, you can connect Google Photos to Gemini Apps to easily access your photos. To connect Google Photos:
On your computer, go to gemini.google.com .
At the bottom, click Settings & help   Personal Intelligence   Connected Apps .

Prompt design is the process of creating prompts, or natural language requests,
that elicit accurate, high quality responses from a language model.
This page introduces basic concepts, strategies, and best practices to get you
started designing prompts to get the most out of Gemini AI models.
Note: Prompt engineering is iterative. These guidelines and templates are
starting points. Experiment and refine based on your specific use cases and
Looking for more specific prompt strategies? Check out our other prompting guides
You can find other sample prompts in the prompt gallery
meant to interactively showcase many of the concepts shared in this guide.
An effective and efficient way to customize model behavior is to provide it with
clear and specific instructions. Instructions can be in the form of a question,
step-by-step tasks, or as complex as mapping out a user's experience and mindset.
Input is the required text in the prompt that you want the model to provide a
response to. Inputs can be a question that the model
answers (question input), a task the model performs (task input), an entity the
model operates on (entity input), or partial input that the model completes or
What's a good name for a flower shop that specializes in selling bouquets of
dried flowers? Create a list of 5 options with just the names.
Here are 5 names for a flower shop specializing in dried flowers:
Give me a simple list of just the things that I must bring on a camping trip. The list should have 5 items.
1. **Tent:** Your shelter from the elements.
2. **Sleeping Bag:** Stay warm and comfortable.
3. **Sleeping Pad:** Insulation and cushioning for a good night's sleep.
4. **Headlamp or Flashlight:** Light for nighttime activities.
5. **First Aid Kit:** Be prepared for minor injuries.

Generative language models work like an advanced auto completion tool. When you
provide partial content, the model can provide the rest of the content or what
it thinks is a continuation of that content as a response. When doing so, if you
include any examples or context, the model can take those examples or context
The following example provides a prompt with an instruction and an entity input:
For the given order, return a JSON object that has the fields cheeseburger, hamburger, fries, or
drink, with the value being the quantity.
Order: A burger and a drink.
While the model did as prompted, writing out the instructions in natural language
can sometimes be challenging and it leaves a lot to the model's interpretation.
For example, a restaurants menu might contain many items. To reduce the size of
the JSON response, you probably want to omit the items that weren't ordered. In

Valid fields are cheeseburger, hamburger, fries, and drink.
Order: Give me a cheeseburger and fries
Order: I want two burgers, a drink, and fries.
Notice how "cheeseburger" was excluded from the output because it wasn't a part

Specify any constraints on reading the prompt or generating a response. You can
tell the model what to do and not to do. For example, you can specify a constraint
in the prompt on how long you want a summary to be:
Summarize this text in one sentence:
Text: A quantum computer exploits quantum mechanical phenomena to perform calculations exponentially
faster than any modern traditional computer. At very tiny scales, physical matter acts as both
particles and as waves, and quantum computing uses specialized hardware to leverage this behavior.
The operating principles of quantum devices is beyond the scope of classical physics. When deployed
at scale, quantum computers could be used in a wide variety of applications such as: in
cybersecurity to break existing encryption methods while helping researchers create new ones, in
meteorology to develop better weather forecasting etc. However, the current state of the art quantum
computers are still largely experimental and impractical.
Exploiting quantum mechanical phenomena, quantum computers can perform calculations exponentially faster than traditional computers for potential applications like cybersecurity and meteorology, although they are currently largely experimental and impractical.
You can give instructions that specify the format of the response. For example,
you can ask for the response to be formatted as a table, bulleted list, elevator
pitch, keywords, sentence, or paragraph. The following system instruction tells
the model to be more conversational in its response:
All questions should be answered comprehensively with details, unless the user requests a concise response specifically.
What is a smart way to make a business that sells DVD's in 2026?
Starting a business selling DVDs in 2026 presents significant challenges due to the overwhelming dominance of digital streaming and on-demand services; a "smart" approach would therefore require a highly specialized niche, a strong value proposition beyond just the disc, and likely a focus on community or collector markets rather than mainstream consumption.
Here's a breakdown of what a smart DVD business in 2026 would likely entail:
1. Extreme Niche Specialization: You cannot compete with streaming libraries. Your business must focus on what digital doesn't offer easily or at all. This could include:
* Out-of-Print & Rare Titles: Sourcing films or TV shows that have never been released digitally or are currently unavailable on major streaming platforms.
